messages:
Sofia Li: heads-up: int8 bring-up for codegen-small (token-optimized) shows divergent regressions on our CodePromptBank. Majority are off-by-one index errors in generated snippets. Not a huge headcount but consistent across languages
Devon Ross: curious — is this a tokenizer alignment issue or quant kernel rounding? Any pattern by language?
Sofia Li: skewed to python and javascript examples that rely on zero-indexing loops. C-like languages fine. Error patterns suggest float->int rounding near boundary conditions when sampling top-p
Marco: can we expand our golden to include boundary-condition cases? propose adding 400 cases focusing on off-by-one, loop-end, and index-edge tests plus 200 language-specific idioms
Asha Patel: yes. also add guidance to labelers: mark whether answer is "functionally correct" vs "textually identical". we'll need both for Pass@1/Pass@k metrics
labeler-bot: scheduled export job: job_id=job_codegen_174512. filters: model=codegen-small-int8-staging, metric=error_delta, top=600, include_golden=true. output s3://redwood-lab/exports/job_codegen_174512.ndjson
Devon Ross: de-dupe plan: use exact code hash then fuzzy AST similarity. keep canonical + up to 4 paraphrases. threshold ast_sim>=0.88. Marco, can you run AST pipeline?
Marco: yep. AST-normalize -> canonicalize variable names -> compute sim. will tag matches and preserve language metadata. will also flag samples with interactive prompts (multi-turn)
Sofia Li: lock eval harness to current seed + sampling (no temp changes). we need deterministic comparison to measure quant impact on correctness and Pass@k
OpsBot: eval harness locked by Sofia Li at 2026-03-15T09:12Z. snapshot id: harness_snapshot_174512
Devon Ross: add micro-golden: 150 synthetic edgecases (variable shadowing, negative indices, slice off-by-one). inject 10 per labeling batch for fast feedback
Asha Patel: labeler instructions: priority to functional tests (unit-style), include minimal test case verifying correctness. in comments, labelers should paste a short test demonstrating correct behavior if they mark incorrect
labeler-bot: export complete, s3://redwood-lab/exports/job_codegen_174512.ndjson checksum: 6f1e2b4c9a7b3f1d2e4c5b6a7d8e9f00. created 24 batches of 25 samples each
Marco: de-dupe finished -> final count 612. pushed 24 batches to code-labeler-queue. marking 8 batches high-priority (boundary-heavy)
Devon Ross: ETA for first pass labeling (12 labelers): 36h. QA runner will sample 10% for unit test verification
Sofia Li: after labels land, run pass@1/pass@5/pass@10 and diff test-case-level failure signals. I want a breakdown by language + failure type (index vs API misuse vs missing import)
Asha Patel: also capture token-latency delta and model size/cost numbers so we can present tradeoffs to PMs. include recommendation: if functional correctness drops >2% we block rolling to Dedicated
Devon Ross: sounds good. I'll create a dashboard tile: codegen_int8_vs_float_pass_rates and add charts for token-latency and per-language failure heatmap
Marco: batches enqueued queue_id=code_q_174512. labeler-bot estimates 36h with current throughput
labeler-bot: micro-golden mg_codegen_174512 injected into first 12 batches
Sofia Li: great. once we have label outputs, let's meet to review top 30 failing test cases and decide whether to tune quant kernels, adjust sampling, or expand training data. thanks!
